title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Auth, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response & Evidence Workflows
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's operational standards for: RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, Secure SDLC controls, security incident response procedures, compliance evidence collection workflows, and the approved process for risk & exceptions. It is intended for engineering, security, product, and compliance stakeholders who operate or audit production and private deployment environments.

Scope

- Applies to Redwood-hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem).
- Covers platform control plane, serving runtime, customer metadata, audit logs, and developer tools.
- Does not replace product-specific privacy policies or customer contractual terms; those are referenced where required.

Principles & Objectives

1. Least privilege: default-deny access and narrow privileges by role.
2. Evidence-first: design systems to generate verifiable audit evidence for compliance requests.
3. Data locality: honor customer-specified residency and retention requirements.
4. Rapid, forensically sound incident response with preserved chain-of-custody.

1) RBAC & Authentication

Summary

Redwood uses role-based access control backed by centralized identity (OIDC + SCIM provisioning for workforce, SAML/SSO for customers where required) and short-lived credentials for service-to-service access.

Authn/Authz Components

- Identity providers: Okta (primary), GCP IAM for cloud service accounts, and customer SAML/OIDC for Private deployments.
- Provisioning: SCIM automated provisioning for standard roles; manual request + approval for elevated roles.
- Enforcement points: API gateway, admin console, infra tooling (Terraform state access), and internal service mesh (mTLS + JWT validation).

Roles and Role Definitions (high level)

- security-admin: full access to security tooling and compliance evidence; emergency-only for incident containment.
- infra-operator: manage cloud infra, autoscaling, and capacity; no access to customer PII by default.
- runtime-engineer: deploy and tune serving runtime; access to model metadata but not customer plaintext data unless approved.
- product-analyst: read-only analytics, aggregated billing, and non-sensitive metrics.

Provisioning & Approval Workflow

1. Request: User requests role via the Access Portal (ServiceNow). Include justification and owner.
2. Approval: Owner_team approver (team lead) must approve. Elevated roles require security review.
3. Time-bound: Elevated access (security-admin, infra-admin) is issued for max 24 hours unless extension approved.
4. Audit: All provisioning events logged to the central audit log (see section 2).

Periodic Review

- Quarterly entitlement review: team leads review membership for their roles.
- Automated orphaned account report monthly: flagged to security ops.

2) Audit Logging Standards

Objectives

- Ensure tamper-evident logs for authentication, authorization changes, configuration changes, and data access events.
- Retain and index logs to satisfy compliance requests and forensic investigations.

What to Log (minimum)

- Authentication: user/service id, identity provider, auth method, success/failure, timestamp, source IP.
- Authorization decisions: resource, action, principal, allowed/denied, reason (policy id).
- Admin actions: role grants/revocations, policy changes, infra changes (Terraform apply), console actions.
- Data access: object id, type, read/write/delete, principal id, request context (query/prompt hash), region.
- System events: deployments, config changes, autoscale events, and service restarts.

Log Integrity & Storage

- Collection: Fluentd/Vector agents forward logs to central log cluster (append-only).
- Integrity: weekly snapshot hashes stored in WORM S3 bucket with KMS-managed keys; daily integrity checks.
- Access: logs are access-controlled; only security and audited infra roles may request raw log exports.

Retention & Tiering

- Short-term (hot): 90 days in ELK/ClickHouse for live investigation and dashboards.
- Mid-term (warm): 1 year archived in compressed object store with index metadata.
- Long-term (cold): up to 7 years for compliance-specific data (by legal/contract).
- Retention exceptions must be approved via the risk & exceptions process.

Alerting & Forensics

- Security signal rules (failed logins, privilege escalations, large data exports) route to PagerDuty and the security slack channel (#sec-ops).
- Forensics runbooks available in "oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks" and include log collection playbooks and query templates.

3) Data Residency & Retention

Policy Summary

- Customer data is stored and processed only in regions explicitly selected at provisioning or contract signature. Default: US and EU regions dependent on customer selection.
- Sensitive data classes (customer PII or regulated data) have stricter controls: encrypted at rest with customer KMS (where configured) and limited export paths.

Data Classification (brief)

- Public: telemetry aggregates, public docs.
- Internal: operational metrics, non-identifying metadata.
- Customer-confidential: customer prompts, model outputs, PII — subject to residency & retention rules.

Retention Schedule (examples)

| Data type | Default retention | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Control plane logs (authz, provisioning) | 7 years | Compliance-grade retention by default |
| Audit logs (access to customer data) | 7 years | Indexed for e-discovery |
| Runtime request traces (raw prompts) | 30 days | Default; longer when customer contract requires |
| Aggregated telemetry | 2 years | Aggregates only, no raw prompts |

Residency Controls & Enforcement

- Region pinning: resources (S3, DBs, compute) are provisioned in the selected region(s) and cross-region replication is disabled unless explicitly authorized.
- Data movement: any export or cross-region copy requires a Data Movement Request (DMR) and DPO approval.

4) Secure SDLC (Secure Software Development Lifecycle)

Goals

- Integrate security gates and evidence generation into the CI/CD pipeline so releases are auditable and reproducible.

Required Controls

- Design: threat modeling for all new services or changes that touch sensitive data; template and reviewer checklist required.
- Code quality: mandatory code review (2 approvers for security-sensitive repos), branch protection, and signed commits for release branches.
- Dependency management: SCA (Snyk/OSS scanner) on every PR; high-risk dependencies blocked until triaged.
- Static/Dynamic testing: SAST on merge to main; DAST on release candidates; container image scanning before deployment.
- Secrets: forbid secrets in code; require HashiCorp Vault or cloud KMS references.
- Build provenance: every production artifact must include build metadata (git SHA, builder image, timestamp).

Release & Rollout Controls

- Canary releases and progressive rollout with automated health & security checks.
- Automatic rollback on security test failures or elevated error budgets.

Developer & Oncall Training

- Mandatory yearly secure-coding training and quarterly tabletop exercises for teams with access to sensitive customer data.

5) Incident Response (Security Procedures)

Objectives

- Detect, contain, eradicate, and recover while preserving evidence and minimizing customer impact.

Incident Classes

- Class 1 (Critical): confirmed customer data exfiltration, production outage impacting >10% customers, active exploitation.
- Class 2 (High): privileged account compromise, significant misconfiguration, or suspected targeted scanning.
- Class 3 (Medium): localized service failure or non-sensitive data exposure.

Response Steps (high-level)

1. Detection & Triage: Security Alerts -> Triage in PagerDuty; assign incident commander (IC).
2. Containment: short-term containment measures (rotate keys, revoke sessions, isolate nodes).
3. Evidence preservation: snapshot affected hosts, export append-only logs, retain network captures in WORM storage.
4. Root cause & eradication: run forensic analysis, apply fixes, patch or revoke compromised credentials.
5. Recovery & Validation: bring services back via tested playbooks; validate with security checks and customer-impact analysis.
6. Post-incident: 72-hour status to stakeholders, full postmortem within 7 business days, actions tracked to closure.

Communications & Escalation

- Internal: #sec-incident Slack channel (private) and all-hands only for Class 1 incidents.
- External: Customer notifications per contract SLA. Legal and PR engaged by Security for Class 1 incidents.

Evidence Handling

- Chain-of-custody must be documented for any pulled artifacts. Forensic artifacts stored with immutable retention and hashed checkpoints.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Purpose

- Provide step-by-step methods for collecting, validating, and delivering evidence for audits (SOC2, ISO27001, regional regulators).

Evidence Owners & Sources

- Access controls evidence: Identity provider logs, SCIM provisioning export, entitlement review records (stored in GCS bucket /evidence/access-control/).
- Change control evidence: Git history, PR approvals, CI build artifacts, Terraform plan/apply logs.
- Logging evidence: indexed audit logs, WORM snapshots, integrity hashes.
- SDLC evidence: threat model artifacts, SAST/DAST reports, dependency scan results.

Collection Process (example SOC2 request)

1. Triage: Compliance requests filed via the Evidence Portal; security assigns an evidence owner.
2. Inventory: owner maps required evidence to known sources using the Evidence Catalog.
3. Pull & Package: export artifacts, include integrity hashes and relevant context (time windows, user ids).
4. Review: security reviews package for completeness; legal reviews if customer-sensitive.
5. Deliver: upload to secure evidence workspace (time-limited link) and record delivery in Evidence Tracker.

Templates & Automation

- Evidence templates maintained in "security-and-compliance/templates" and automated pulls for common requests (entitlement lists, log slices) via internal tooling.

SLA for Requests

- Routine requests: 5 business days.
- Priority (audit kickoff): 48 hours initial package and 10 business days for complete artifacts.

7) Risk & Exceptions

When to use

- Exceptions are required when a standard control cannot be implemented within acceptable time/cost or conflicts with customer contractual requirements.

Exceptions Process

1. Submit: complete the Risk & Exception form with scope, compensating controls, estimated duration, and owner.
2. Review: security and affected owners review risk; privacy/legal if customer data impacted.
3. Approve: executive security approver (CISO or delegated) signs off; high-risk exceptions require Board notification if >90 days.
4. Monitor: approved exceptions are tracked with automated reminders and reviewed monthly.

Compensating Controls (examples)

- If region pinning cannot be immediately enforced, require end-to-end encryption using customer-managed keys and restrict access to a small allowlist of hosts.
- If a legacy dependency cannot be removed quickly, isolate service in a hardened subnet, apply strict egress rules, and increase monitoring.

Appendices

A. Relevant Links

- Identity & Access runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/identity-access-runbook
- Log collection standard: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/log-collection-standards
- Evidence templates: /confluence/security-and-compliance/templates/evidence-templates

B. Minimum SLOs & Thresholds

- Audit log collection latency: 2 minutes (99th percentile) from event -> indexed.
- RBAC provisioning turnaround: 48 hours for standard requests; emergency requests handled within 4 hours.
- Incident response MTTR (Class 1): target 4 hours to containment.
